PullRequest.Title: Fix clicks just below an empty line not focusing the editor
PullRequest.Body:
Clicking an empty editor just below its only line can be silently ignored: the cursor isn't placed and the editor doesn't get focus. The empty chat input in the Agents window hits this at the vertical middle of the input box, where its single line ends, and repeated trackpad taps keep landing in the same spot.

There is no existing issue for this; it was traced live in the Agents window.

## Root cause

The chat input editor sits at a fractional page offset (869.025px in the traced window). Its empty line spans vertical offsets 12 to 32 (12px top padding, 20px line height), so its bottom edge is at 901.025px.

- Chromium paints and hit tests the composited lines layer (`.lines-content`, which has a 3D transform) at whole pixels. A click at y = 901 therefore lands below the painted line, and the event targets the `.view-lines` container instead of a `.view-line`.
- The editor's mouse math uses the unrounded position from `getBoundingClientRect`: 901 − 869.025 = 31.975, which is inside line 1 and not yet in the bottom padding (which starts at 32).
- `MouseTargetFactory._hitTestViewLines` has a branch for events that target the `.view-lines` container itself, but only the GPU renderer used it. With the DOM renderer, the event falls through to the `caretRangeFromPoint` hit test. An empty line has no text node, the hit test still reports the `.view-lines` container (so there is no retry with another target), and the result is `fulfillUnknown()`.
- `MouseHandler._onMouseDown` only prevents the default and calls `focusTextArea()` for content targets, so an `UNKNOWN` target does nothing.

The traced trackpad events had `clientY` 901 (truncated from a pointer position of 901.99), so every tap at that resting position was ignored. In the same window, a click inside the line focused the editor.

## Fix

Move the empty-line check of the `.view-lines` container branch out of its GPU-only condition. When the event targets the container and the line under the mouse (per the editor's layout) is empty, both renderers now return an empty content target at column 1 of that line, the same result as an event that targets the empty `.view-line` itself.

What this does and doesn't change:

- It only runs when the event targets the `.view-lines` container itself, after the top padding, bottom padding and after-the-last-line cases have returned, so the line is the one under the mouse, not necessarily the last line.
- Only empty lines are affected. Lines with text still go through the DOM hit test.
- The GPU renderer runs the same check in the same order as before.
- Where the DOM hit test used to succeed for an empty line under the container (by retrying with the `.view-line` it found), the result is the same empty content target at column 1; it is now returned without the hit test.

## How to test

The new unit test reproduces the geometry: an editor at a 0.1px page offset with the same padding and line height, and a mouse down on the first whole pixel below its empty line, dispatched to `.view-lines` as Chromium does.

Commands, run in a fresh worktree on `main`:

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` (with `mouseTarget.ts` from `main`) — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/codeEditorWidget.test.ts --grep "just below an empty line"` (with `mouseTarget.ts` from `main`) — **failed as expected**: the mouse target was `{ type: 0 (UNKNOWN), position: null }`
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` (with the fix) — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/codeEditorWidget.test.ts` — passed (17 passing, 1 pending; the pending IME test skips when the test window lacks focus)
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/editor/test/browser/**/*.test.js"` — passed
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/editor/browser/controller/mouseTarget.ts src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/codeEditorWidget.test.ts` — passed
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed

In the traced window, replaying the same mouse down with the fix applied focused the chat input. Manually, the band is about 1px tall, so it's hard to hit on purpose. With an empty chat input, rest the pointer just below the placeholder line (the vertical middle of the input box) and tap. Without the fix, some resting positions never focus the input; with the fix, every tap does.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clicking or hovering at a fractional-pixel edge of an empty DOM-rendered editor line, including an empty chat input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MouseHandler._createMouseTarget synchronously calls MouseTargetFactory._hitTestViewLines before mouse event emission and, on mouse down, focus and selection. The new branch resolves one line, checks its length, reads its width, and returns CONTENT_EMPTY without evaluating the lazy DOM caret hit test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously flush pending editor rendering and obtain the single rendered line width; the general renderer can read offsetWidth on a cold width cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One width request per qualifying empty-line hit; clean render state returns immediately. Fast monospace empty lines compute width arithmetically; the general renderer reads offsetWidth only until its width cache is populated or invalidated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: DOM container hits did not enter this width branch directly. They performed caret hit testing and could retry through the existing strict-child branch, which already reads the same width. GPU container hits already used this width branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before mouse handling can focus or emit the event. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added or reached by the changed hit-test helpers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser caretRangeFromPoint/caretPositionFromPoint and optional shadow-root hit testing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one Gecko caret query or up to two Chromium caret queries per lazy hit-test evaluation; now none when the event supplies the container target and the line is empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The empty DOM-container scenario fell through to lazy browser hit testing, sometimes followed by target switching. This PR bypasses that work for the empty line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new early return avoids these browser hit-testing calls before mouse handling progresses.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One line under the pointer per handled mouse event, not all document lines. Vertical line lookup uses binary search; line length uses projection metadata or piece-tree offset lookups. Dirty rendering, if needed, covers the existing viewport and dirty view parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser UI-thread execution; no asynchronous fan-out or new queue. Rendering respects existing dirty-state suppression.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: HitTestRequest retains one lazy hit-test result and target-path cache for the request only. Existing line width caching and render dirty flags are preserved. Warm ordinary empty lines require no width DOM read and no repaint; cold general-renderer widths can require one cached geometry read. No new persistent cache or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-line call path, width-cache behavior, dirty-render guards, and removal of lazy caret testing, supported by the changed branch and helper implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of fractional-edge events and occurrence of dirty views or decorated/proportional empty lines are unmeasured. Neither a repeated full-render mechanism nor an expensive collection-wide addition is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The bounded additional width path supports the intended empty-content hit behavior, reuses the normal empty-line handler, and skips browser caret work; there is no evidence of newly repeated or unbounded expensive work.

Scenarios.Scenario: DOM-rendered nonempty-line container hits and ordinary line-child, padding, or view-zone hits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hit testing completes before hover/context-menu/mouse-down dispatch. Nonempty container hits now perform a line-number and length check, then retain the existing lazy DOM hit test. Strict-child, top/bottom-padding, and earlier view-zone paths remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing browser caret hit testing and, for content results, synchronous pending-render flush and DOM position/width resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-request lazy result is evaluated once, with up to two Chromium caret queries; retry can reuse that same hit-test result. The diff does not change this boundary count for nonempty lines.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Nonempty DOM container hits already fell through to the same browser hit test and content resolution. Ordinary child and padding branches performed their existing checks and returned their existing targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains synchronous and on the event path, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One line lookup and one length lookup per nonempty container hit. No scan or copy of line text is introduced; normal line children and padding do not enter the changed branch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread input handling; no new asynchronous work, parallelism, or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing request-local lazy hit-test caching and rendered-line width caches remain intact. The added length check uses existing projection metadata or piece-tree offset queries rather than materializing text.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from explicit branch conditions, binary-search vertical lookup, view-model length implementation, and unchanged downstream hit-test code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings collected for the extra logarithmic lookup, but the diff does not add a heavyweight boundary for nonempty container hits.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: only bounded metadata lookups are added to this container case, with no amplification of existing expensive boundaries.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same line-number, empty-line, width, RTL, and coordinate-resolution checks execute synchronously before dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing pending-render flush, GPU viewport-derived width/position computation, and possible DOM-width fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same one width request for a qualifying GPU container hit, followed by existing coordinate computation when needed. No extra call is introduced by moving the empty-line check outside the GPU condition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The GPU-only branch already looked up the line, checked its length, and handled empty lines before nonempty width/RTL/position checks. The diff preserves that sequence and cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target line per event. Existing nonempty GPU coordinate resolution can scan that line's content, but its frequency and input are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous UI-thread target computation; GPU rendering ownership and scheduling remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing GPU viewport/render-option state and DOM fallback width caches are unchanged; cold initialization and warm behavior are not modified.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct before/after comparison and the GPU width and coordinate helper implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing line-length-dependent GPU computation is not measured, but no causal change to its cost is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: GPU execution order and expensive-work cardinality are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: New isolated browser widget test for fractional-offset empty-line mouse targeting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test constructs one editor, attaches one empty model, renders once, dispatches three input events, and asserts the captured mouse-down target. This path is not production startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attach a DOM container, explicitly layout/render the test editor, read one bounding rectangle, and dispatch synthetic input events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One editor construction and explicit render, one bounding-rectangle read, and three event dispatches per test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This test was absent; production editor startup and rendering paths were not changed by the test addition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local synchronous work on the browser test path only. No new production subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed-size editor, one empty line, one listener, and one captured target per test invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous test body; no new parallel editor creation or background operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All editor/model/listener objects are registered in the suite disposal store, and container removal is registered explicitly. The captured target array remains test-local; no lifetime-expanding cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete test diff and suite disposal setup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Incremental test-suite duration is not measured; the fixed-size fixture does not establish a scaling regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or retained-resource mechanism in the test addition.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the full two-file inventory and every diff page against base bfbf12b35b9978b92b2d341e81ade49f2b18c68c. Traced DOM/GPU hit-test callers, browser geometry boundaries, render dirty guards, line lookup/length implementations, width-cache behavior, and test resource ownership. No high-confidence introduced performance issue or independently substantiated historical performance-regression fix was found; no findings or fix-learning records submitted. Static review only. The supporting performance guide was requested but its tool response exceeded the output limit; learned-regression guidance was fully available.
